title: Design serverless and batch compute
learningObjective: Recommend serverless solutions (Functions, Durable Functions, Logic Apps, Container Apps) and batch processing solutions (Azure Batch, Container Apps jobs, Spot capacity).
foundation: Serverless means you write code or a workflow and Azure runs it only when something happens. You pay for what runs.
Batch processing means running lots of work in parallel, such as thousands of simulations overnight.
engineer: Azure Functions: event-driven code (HTTP, timers, queues, Event Grid, Event Hubs, Cosmos DB change feed). Hosting: Flex Consumption (recommended serverless plan: fast scale, scale to zero, VNet integration, always-ready instances), Premium (pre-warmed instances, longer runs), Dedicated (App Service plan). Durable Functions add stateful orchestration: function chaining, fan-out/fan-in, async HTTP APIs, monitors and human interaction.

Azure Logic Apps: low-code workflows with hundreds of managed connectors (Microsoft 365, SAP, Salesforce), Consumption (multi-tenant, pay per action) or Standard (single-tenant, VNet integration, stateful and stateless workflows). Good for integration owned by citizen developers or integration teams.

Batch: Azure Batch schedules large parallel and HPC workloads on pools of VMs (including Spot/low-priority nodes and GPU or HPC sizes) with job and task management and auto-scaling formulas; Container Apps jobs run containerised tasks on demand, on a schedule or triggered by events; HPC options include H-series VMs with InfiniBand and Azure Managed Lustre storage.

animation.caption: Choose Functions, Durable Functions, Logic Apps, Batch or Container Apps jobs.

example.title: An insurance claims pipeline
body: Uploaded claim photos trigger a function that resizes and classifies them. A Durable Functions orchestration waits for an assessor's approval, then pays out.
A Logic App posts approved claims to Teams and the finance SAP system. Monthly risk simulations run on Azure Batch with Spot nodes.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: Function App > Create: hosting plan (Flex Consumption / Premium / Dedicated).
Logic App > Create: Consumption or Standard.
Batch account > Pools: VM size, Spot nodes, autoscale formula.
configuration.cli:
az functionapp create -g rg-app -n func-claims --storage-account stclaims --flexconsumption-location westeurope --runtime dotnet-isolated --runtime-version 8.0
az batch pool create --id pool-sim --vm-size Standard_D4s_v5 --target-low-priority-nodes 50 --image canonical:0001-com-ubuntu-server-jammy:22_04-lts --node-agent-sku-id "batch.node.ubuntu 22.04"
configuration.powershell: New-AzFunctionApp -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name func-claims -StorageAccountName stclaims -Runtime DotNet -FunctionsVersion 4 -Location westeurope

lab.objective: Pick the serverless or batch service.
expected: Durable Functions for long-running stateful flows

validation.text: Chose the right serverless or batch service

failureScenarios: Using a timer loop in a function to wait for approval
Running HPC jobs on one big VM
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: A function times out waiting for an external approval.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a Durable Functions orchestration with an external event.

troubleshooting.symptom: Batch jobs take too long to start each night.
troubleshooting.fix: Use an autoscale formula that pre-provisions before the job window.

comparisons.difference: Functions: code-first; Logic Apps: designer-first with connectors.

comparisons.service: Azure Batch vs Container Apps jobs
comparisons.difference: Batch: large VM pools and HPC scheduling; Container Apps jobs: containerised tasks without managing pools.

misconceptions.reality: Plans have execution, scale and memory limits.

misconceptions.myth: Logic Apps can't run in a VNet.
misconceptions.reality: Logic Apps Standard supports VNet integration.

architectureDecisions: Flex Consumption Functions for event-driven code.
Batch (with Spot) for large parallel jobs.

verification.notes: Drafted by AI and checked against the linked official documentation. Not yet reviewed by a human subject-matter expert.

walkthrough.subtitle: Run code only when something happens, and run huge parallel jobs without managing servers.

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Work that comes and goes
body: Photos arrive at random, approvals take days, and simulations need 1,000 cores once a month.

steps.label: Functions
steps.title: Code that runs on events
body: A function wakes up for each event and scales out with load. The Flex Consumption plan scales fast, can scale to zero, and supports VNet integration.

steps.label: Workflows
steps.title: State and integration
body: Durable Functions remember where they are, so an order can wait days for approval. Logic Apps build workflows in a designer with hundreds of connectors.

steps.label: Batch
steps.title: Thousands of tasks in parallel
body: Azure Batch creates a pool of VMs, runs the tasks and scales the pool away. Spot nodes cut cost for work that can be retried.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Serverless and batch
recap: Durable Functions for state; Logic Apps for connectors
